incidents.victim: Education, transportation, healthcare and financial firms (multi-continent)
incidents.vector: Microsoft Threat Intelligence detailed 'The Gentlemen', a Go-based ransomware-as-a-service that uses XChaCha20 with per-file Curve25519 keys and aggressive self-propagation, spawning SYSTEM-privileged child processes to encrypt local volumes and network shares simultaneously.
incidents.impact: The RaaS program — which moved from a closed group to broad affiliate recruitment and just partnered with BreachForums to bring in initial access brokers and pen-testers — has hit organizations across North America, South America, Europe, Africa and Asia, combining double extortion with data exfiltration for public-leak pressure.

incidents.victim: Zapier (8,000+ third-party integrations, millions of users)
incidents.vector: Token Security chained five separate weaknesses — starting from a free Zapier account — that exposed login credentials, an internal storage system holding 1,100+ private images, and ultimately a publishing key for code that runs inside every signed-in Zapier user's browser.
incidents.impact: If discovered first by a malicious actor, the chain would have enabled supply-chain compromise across millions of accounts and the customer systems Zapier connects to; researchers also demonstrated the ability to send email from a third-party AI company CTO's Gmail. Zapier triaged in four days, patched in three weeks, and paid the $3,000 maximum bounty.

incidents.vector: FBI warned that the Silent Ransom Group (also tracked as Luna Moth, Chatty Spider, UNC3753 and Storm-0252) impersonates internal IT staff via phone and phishing email to gain remote access, and when that fails sends an operative to the victim's office to physically plug a storage device into a workstation and copy files.
incidents.impact: The Russia-based group, active since 2022 with more than 100 claimed attacks, has surged activity in recent months against law firms — exfiltrating client data to leak sites and demanding ransoms to suppress publication. The legal sector was the fourth most-targeted industry by ransomware actors in Q1 2026.

incidents.vector: Dutch financial-crime investigators (FIOD) arrested MIRhosting owner Andrey Nesterenko (39) and Amsterdam-based Youssef Zinad (57) on May 18 for violating EU sanctions by providing connectivity to entities hosting Russia-linked cyber and influence operations.
incidents.impact: FIOD raided three businesses and two data centres in Enschede, Almere, Dronten and Schiphol-Rijk, seizing laptops, phones and more than 800 servers; customer data on those servers was lost. The seizure cuts off the last major Stark Industries upstream provider after May 2025 EU sanctions against PQHosting, and follows reporting that WorkTitans/MIRhosting carried the heaviest pro-Russian attack traffic against Danish government bodies during the November 2025 municipal elections.

incidents.victim: Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (LACMTA)
incidents.vector: Iranian operators posing as a hacktivist crew named 'Ababil of Minab' breached LACMTA in mid-March, then used scripts and hands-on-keyboard actions to wipe databases, virtual machines, backups and storage volumes.
incidents.impact: At least 700 GB of email, backups and other files were exfiltrated and parts of the transit network were forced offline; Israeli researchers at Gambit Security tied the group to Iran's intelligence service after data was inadvertently exposed online, adding forensic backing to the long-suspected state link.

incidents.victim: Tri-Rail (South Florida commuter rail) and Vyncs (vehicle tracking)
incidents.vector: The Iran-linked 'Ababil of Minab' persona — the same group behind the LACMTA wiper attack — also claimed responsibility for breaches at Tri-Rail and at vehicle tracking company Vyncs, which detected its intrusion on April 2.
incidents.impact: Tri-Rail confirmed a hack but said no critical data was affected; Vyncs owner Agnik declined to characterize the stolen data and is working with the FBI. The cluster of US transportation-sector hits underscores expanded Iranian targeting of transit and mobility infrastructure.

incidents.victim: Unimac (Saudi infrastructure firm) and additional regional targets
incidents.vector: The same Iran-MOIS persona ('Ababil of Minab') breached Saudi infrastructure firm Unimac and additional unnamed victims including an Israeli media organization, an Israeli university and a Turkish insurance brokerage.
incidents.impact: Data was exfiltrated from each target; Unimac did not respond to requests for comment, and the broader campaign demonstrates Iran's continued use of fake-hacktivist personas to target regional adversaries and critical infrastructure.

incidents.vector: Attackers believed affiliated with the Chinese government used phishing to access Microsoft 365 mailboxes of Wiley Rein personnel between July 2024 and June 2025 before the firm detected the intrusion last year; the proposed class action alleges MFA and basic safeguards were absent.
incidents.impact: Names, addresses, dates of birth, financial account numbers, medical information and Social Security numbers were stolen; the firm only began notifying victims on or around March 6, 2026, and is now facing a proposed class action in DC federal court (Burkett v. Wiley Rein, No. 26-cv-1791). The named plaintiff says he suffered at least 19 fraudulent charges to a MetLife estate account following the breach.

incidents.vector: UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office sanctioned Huobi Global SA — the Panamanian operator of HTX — and 17 other entities for forming part of the infrastructure used by Russia to circumvent sanctions imposed to stymie its war effort.
incidents.impact: UK authorities allege HTX helped move approximately $1.5 billion back to the Kremlin; the action is the latest UK move to close crypto-based sanctions-evasion channels tied to Russian state actors.

incidents.vector: A six-hour automated campaign codenamed 'Megalodon' used dummy accounts and forged author identities to push 5,718 malicious commits into 5,561 GitHub repositories on May 18, injecting GitHub Actions workflows that exfiltrate CI/CD secrets, cloud credentials, SSH keys, OpenID Connect tokens and source code secrets.
incidents.impact: A second-stage payload replaces existing workflows with a dormant 'workflow-dispatch' backdoor that produces no visible CI runs; researchers say roughly 83% of affected repos remained infected more than a week later, and downstream npm package @tiledesk/tiledesk-server was poisoned and republished to users. Similarities to TeamPCP's Shai-Hulud worm have been noted but attribution remains unconfirmed.

incidents.vector: Operators ran SEO poisoning that placed lookalike download sites for CrystalDiskInfo, HWMonitor, FurMark, K-Lite Codec Pack and other utilities in search results and — newly — in AI chatbot responses; victims downloaded ZIPs from gleeze.com subdomains that delivered crypto-mining payloads alongside ScreenConnect remote-access agents.
incidents.impact: Microsoft Defender Experts blocked the campaign but warns the persistent ScreenConnect footprint could later be repurposed for data theft, lateral movement or ransomware; the operator deliberately targets high-end GPU systems to maximize mining yield per host and is among the first publicly reported cases of LLM-assisted malware delivery.

incidents.vector: A Nightwing contractor administering CISA's code platform created a public GitHub repo called 'Private-CISA' in November 2025 and intentionally disabled GitHub's built-in secret-scanning protection, exposing AWS GovCloud admin keys, plaintext passwords for dozens of internal CISA systems, and an RSA private key for a CISA-IT GitHub app with full access to every repo in the CISA-IT organization.
incidents.impact: More than a week after notification CISA was still rotating leaked credentials; Senator Maggie Hassan and Reps. Bennie Thompson and Delia Ramirez demanded answers, warning the exposure handed China, Russia and Iran a roadmap into federal networks during a period of major CISA workforce cuts. TruffleHog's creator confirmed CISA only revoked the GitHub app key after additional notification on May 20.

incidents.victim: Kimwolf DDoS botnet (millions of IoT devices)
incidents.vector: Canadian police arrested Jacob Butler ('Dort'), 23, of Ottawa on a US extradition warrant; he allegedly built and rented an IoT botnet that enslaved millions of cameras, photo frames and similar devices, generating record DDoS attacks measured near 30 Tbps including hits against US Department of Defense IP ranges.
incidents.impact: Some victims incurred losses exceeding $1 million and the botnet issued over 25,000 attack commands; March 19 takedowns dismantled the technical infrastructure of Kimwolf and three competing botnets (Aisuru, JackSkid, Mossad). Butler also faces charges for swatting attacks against researchers who helped unmask him.

incidents.victim: Dozens of organizations in US, UK, Australia (M365/Okta tenants)
incidents.vector: Threat actor UNC6671 ('BlackFile') runs high-volume voice phishing against employees' personal phones, posing as IT for a passkey/MFA migration and steering them to lookalike SSO portals on enrollms[.]com, passkeyms[.]com and setupsso[.]com to harvest credentials and MFA codes in real time via an adversary-in-the-middle proxy.
incidents.impact: Google Threat Intelligence Group says dozens of organizations have been compromised and had M365, SharePoint, OneDrive, Zendesk and Salesforce data exfiltrated for extortion; UNC6671 has at times misused the ShinyHunters brand to add credibility to extortion threats and now runs a dedicated 'BlackFile' data leak site.
